precepts.text: Consider that I labor not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning. Captains left at 4 a.m. to teach and check the congregation; bishops and deacons travel the world. Be nation-minded, not me, me, me.
precepts.point: Because he asked understanding and not long life, riches, or the life of his enemies, God gave him a wise and understanding heart like none before or after. When your mind is for the people, the Lord blesses beyond measure and gives more than you desired.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
Solomon’s mind was on the people. He did not ask for four hundred women or chariots, or to be a king of 4,000; he asked for “an understanding heart to judge thy people”, “for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?” Because he had a mind for the people, the Lord elevated him and gave him more than he even desired for himself. Likewise with us: when we have a mind for the people, the Lord will bless that thing beyond measure.

Sirach says it plainly: “Consider that I laboured not for myself only, but for all them that seek learning.” In this truth we are not doing this for ourselves. Captains left at four in the morning, driving, so they could be here to help teach the class. A captain drove down and got here at five in the morning to check the congregation, to check on the saints of the Most High. The bishops travel all over the world; the deacons travel. This is not for ourselves; this is for the nation of Israel, because we understand the kingdom that is at hand.

“but for all them”: this is a nation. You must be nation-minded. A lot of times we are not like that: me, me, me, me, me, and that is all you are concerned with. But all through the Bible the greatest leaders were focused on the nation of Israel and how to move the nation further ahead.

That is the mindset of a leader and the action of a king: like Solomon, labour not for yourself only, but for all the people, and the Lord gives more than you asked.

precepts.text: Solomon loved the Lord and asked for an understanding heart to discern between good and bad; the speech pleased the Lord, who gave him a wise heart like none before or after, and also riches and honour he had not asked for.
precepts.point: Solomon as a youth asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, not long life, riches, or his enemies' lives, and the Lord gave him what he did not ask as well. Seek ye first the kingdom and the rest is added. Wisdom of Solomon 7:6-13: he preferred her before sceptres and thrones, loved her above health and beauty, and did not hide her riches; Sirach 4:23, hide not thy wisdom in her beauty. Our conversation should be in the scriptures.
precepts.why:
We have to be like Solomon: we have to pray for wisdom so that we can be increased. “And Solomon loved the Lord, walking in the statutes of David his father”, and at Gibeon “the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.”

Solomon answered, “I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in”, set in the midst of “a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.” “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad”. As a youth, Solomon understood that wisdom was important. He could have asked for a lot of different things, but he asked for wisdom.

“And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.” Because he “hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies”, God gave him “a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.” And more: “I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour”.

The Lord gave Solomon things he did not ask for because he asked for the right thing. We can desire different pleasures of lust, but seek ye first the kingdom of heaven and everything else will be added to us. Take a page out of Solomon’s book: wisdom exalted him because he sought her.

precepts.text: David felt his own iniquities as a burden too heavy and leaned on the Lord — show me where I am wrong. A lot of you take correction and then pray the Lord judge the man who corrected you.
precepts.point: Wisdom came as a gift and became a trial: the same man wrote that increasing knowledge increases sorrow. It can crush you or make you rise.

precepts.text: The saints shall judge the world and even angels, so those in the church should be able to judge the smallest matters of this life.
precepts.point: This is what we still need to pray for. We should pray that the Most High endows our leadership with wisdom, and that we ourselves learn wisdom in these scriptures and how to judge matters among one another.

note.label: 1 Kings 3: Solomon Asks for Wisdom to Judge

precepts.why:
“Dare any of you, having a matter against another, go to law before the unjust, and not before the saints? Do ye not know that the saints shall judge the world? and if the world shall be judged by you, are ye unworthy to judge the smallest matters? Know ye not that we shall judge angels? how much more things that pertain to this life?”

The saints shall judge the world and even angels, so those in the church should be able to judge the smallest matters of this life. That is why Solomon’s request is ours too. He asked, “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad”.

This is what we still need to pray for: that the Most High endows our leadership with wisdom, and that we ourselves learn wisdom in these scriptures and how to judge matters among one another.

precepts.text: The Most High exalts the horn of his people, the children of Israel, a people near unto him, who are the saints.
precepts.point: This is what we still need to pray for. We should pray that the Most High endows our leadership with wisdom, and that we ourselves learn wisdom in these scriptures and how to judge matters among one another.

note.label: 1 Kings 3: Solomon Asks for Wisdom to Judge

precepts.why:
“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.”

The saints are the children of Israel, a people near unto him. So when Paul says the saints shall judge the world, it is Israel that will judge. That is the great people Solomon stood in the midst of, “thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude”, and the people he asked for an understanding heart to judge.

precepts.text: Solomon said the Lord had made him king in the room of David his father, though he was but a little child that knew not how to go out or come in.
precepts.point: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.
precepts.why:
First Kings 3 tells the same night, where the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and gives more detail of what was said. Solomon said: “And now, O Lord my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in.”

That is what he meant in Chronicles: “Give me now wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people.” He knew he was not able to go out and come in before them on his own. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.

precepts.text: Solomon asked for an understanding heart to judge the people, that he might discern between good and bad.
precepts.point: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.
precepts.why:
“Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?”

This is the same request as in Chronicles: “Give me now wisdom and knowledge … for who can judge this thy people, that is so great?” Kings shows what the wisdom was for: an understanding heart, to discern between good and bad, and to judge a people “like the dust of the earth in multitude.”

precepts.text: The speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.
precepts.point: Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge that he might go out and come in before the people, for who could judge so great a people. When you read between Kings and Chronicles and line up the history, you get the full detail of what went on with Solomon and David.
precepts.why:
“And the speech pleased the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.”

The Most High had said, “Ask what I shall give thee”, and Solomon asked for wisdom and knowledge to judge the people. That request pleased the Lord. Kings supplies this detail that Chronicles leaves out.

note.label: 1 Kings 3: Solomon Asks for Wisdom to Judge

points: Because Solomon asked for understanding to discern judgment and not for long life, riches, or the life of his enemies, the Most High gives him a wise and understanding heart like no other before or after. He also gives what Solomon did not ask, riches and honor, and promises length of days if he walks in his ways.

note.label: 1 Kings 3: Solomon Asks for Wisdom to Judge

points: Two harlots come before the king, each claiming the living child, after one woman's child died in the night and she exchanged it. Solomon calls for a sword and commands the living child divided in two, and gives half to each.

note.label: 1 Kings 3: Solomon Asks for Wisdom to Judge

points: The true mother pleads that the child be given alive to the other rather than slain, and by this the king discerns her, for her bowels yearned upon her son. All Israel hears the judgment and fears the king, for they see the wisdom of God is in him to do judgment.
